questions.reasoning_anchor: A singular 2 by 2 matrix has linearly dependent columns.
For a 3 by 3 matrix, det(5A) = 5^3 det(A), not 5 det(A).
A^T A is positive semidefinite, so its determinant is nonnegative.
Cramer's rule requires a nonzero coefficient determinant.

questions.reference_method: One efficient exemplar uses determinant-aware elementary row operations.
questions.accepted_method_policy: This exemplar is not a required method. Any valid determinant computation, including direct expansion, determinant properties, row or column transformations, triangularization, or another equivalent route, is acceptable.

questions.reference_derivation: A unique solution exists exactly when det(A) = s^2 + 8s = s(s + 8) is nonzero.
questions.expected_result: s is not equal to 0 or -8
questions.accepted_method_policy: The determinant condition and a valid row-reduction or elimination argument are both acceptable. Other mathematically valid arguments establishing the same exclusion set are also acceptable.

questions.reference_derivation: Using p0 as a common vertex gives edge vectors (1, 4, 1), (0, 1, -2), and (-2, 1, 1). Their scalar triple product has absolute value 21, so the tetrahedron volume is |21| / 6 = 7/2.
questions.accepted_method_policy: A valid scalar-triple-product, determinant, base-times-height, or equivalent coordinate-geometry derivation is acceptable.
